conventions.title: Price year
conventions.statement: Money is at the prices of 2025.

conventions.title: Accounting window
conventions.statement: The accounting of a scenario covers 43,800 h, five years of 8,760 h, from the start.

conventions.title: Year one
conventions.statement: The first year of a scenario is its first 8,760 h.

conventions.title: Time origin
conventions.statement: Elapsed hours begin at the scheduled initiating cyber action; the initiating effect follows it as declared in `initiation`.

conventions.title: Conditioning
conventions.statement: Each scenario is conditional on the initiating action executing; no attack probability is modeled.

conventions.title: Interpolation
conventions.statement: Report samples evaluate the retained continuous trajectory; display sampling does not define integration or event times.

conventions.title: Counting
conventions.statement: Deaths and casualties count unique people, and economic loss counts losses that do not overlap.

values.deaths: Unique people whose deaths the event caused or accelerated within five years.
values.casualties: Unique people counted at first death or qualifying serious harm. At a reporting instant: cumulative unique casualties = cumulative deaths + living people already counted as casualties, if the declared cohort scope is closed. Eventual serious survivors are a distinct end-horizon measure.
values.economic_loss: Non-overlapping damaged assets, incremental response resources, output not made up later, qualifying unrecovered principal.

conventions.title: Hazus casualty severity levels
conventions.statement: Casualties use the Hazus casualty severity levels: S1, basic medical aid; S2, hospital care, not life-threatening; S3, life-threatening without prompt care; S4, killed or mortally injured. A death is S4, and serious harm is S3 with lasting impairment.

conventions.title: Time units
conventions.statement: Fixed model day=24 h; year=365 days; month=year/12. No implicit calendar or currency/price-year conversions.

conventions.title: Evidence
conventions.statement: A verified source claim confirms only the recorded fact and scope. Model transfers, illustrative assumptions, and parameter bounds need independent justification. Unverified and partial claims remain visibly qualified.
